_comment: v3.66.1242 row-228 battery. The gate it replaces asks whether the two optional-capability function names appear in COMMAND POSITION in the provisioner's text; the replacement SOURCES the shipped script into an instrumented bash shell and reads what the running shell did. M1-M3 attack the SUBJECT -- delete the dispatch, regrade it core, stop sourcing the library -- and each must be seen by the behavioural half rather than by a scan. M4-M6 attack three rules of the battery ITSELF that would otherwise be unnamed: that a call reached from OUTSIDE any run_step is not graded, that two capabilities may not share one run_step row, and that a run which dispatches and then exits before the verdict has told the operator nothing. O1 is the anti-brittleness control, and it pins a defect this cut actually shipped and then fixed: the first implementation required the run_step COMMAND WORD to be the function name, which is a spelling and not a behaviour -- the dispatched-through-a-wrapper fixture caught it on the first run, and a variable, a wrapper and an eval are all correct provisioners it would have rejected. RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the over-sensitivity control found that defect before the mutation battery did, and the three battery rules M4-M6 pin were added afterwards precisely because nothing in the file named them.  SECOND PASS, recorded because a clean first battery is a reason to look harder: M1-M6 and O1 were 7 caught 0 escaped on the first run, and probing three rules of the harness ITSELF that no test named then found a real defect in this cut's own code. The instrumented run_step's unset-argument guard is written inside a Python f-string, where `${1:-}` is a FORMAT FIELD rather than shell text -- it rendered as the digit 1, the generated bash read `case "$1" in`, and under the provisioner's own `set -u` a run_step handed no command would have aborted the entire instrumented run, which is indistinguishable from the evasions this file rejects. M9 is that rule, now named and caught; the test written for it immediately found a SECOND unguarded `$1` on the next line. M7 and M8 are the other two unnamed rules: that the harness really EXECUTES what it records, and that its reading of the existing text gate is not fail-open (a vacuous [] would make every evasion claim in the file meaningless). DELIBERATELY NOT MUTATED, and named rather than omitted silently: the `readonly -f` protection over the two capability recorders. Removing it makes the run execute the library's REAL bodies, which talk to a live PostgreSQL and write into the invoking user's home -- a mutation battery must not provision the host it runs on. That rule is asserted directly instead, from both sides, by test_the_recorder_and_not_the_real_body_is_what_ran, and its refusal was proved able to FIRE on this host with a harmless stub library standing in for the real one.
subject: v3.66.1242 -- the provisioner's optional capabilities are judged by what the shell dispatched, not by where their names sit in the text

mutants.label: M1 the mod3 capability is never dispatched: the graded step runs nothing while the name still stands in command position elsewhere in the file
M2 the dev-inspect capability is graded core, so a host that cannot install an OPTIONAL seam fails provisioning instead of warning
M3 the shared library is mentioned but never sourced, so on a real host both capability names resolve to nothing while every text arm stays green
M4 a capability reached from outside any run_step counts as dispatched, so its outcome is never graded, logged or reported and the gate says nothing
M5 two capabilities may share one run_step, so one WARN row covers both and a host missing exactly one cannot be told from a host missing neither
mutants.new: if False and call.slug in graded:

mutants.label: M6 a run that dispatches and then exits before the verdict passes, so a missing capability is provisioned-around in silence -- backlog row 96's original state
M7 the instrumented run_step records commands but executes none of them, so 'the dispatch reached the function' is never actually measured
M8 the reading of the existing text gate goes fail-open, so every 'this fixture evades the scan' claim in the file becomes vacuous
M9 the instrumentation drops its unset-argument guard, so a run_step handed no command aborts the whole instrumented run and the abort reads as an evasion of the subject

O1 the dispatch must be spelled with the function name as the run_step command word, so a wrapper, a variable or an eval is rejected -- the spelling rule this cut shipped first and the wrapper fixture caught
